newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW-Snam Progetti drops out of Pemex project.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Snam Progetti drops out of Pemex project.

text.p: Italian construction company Snam Progetti has dropped out of the running for a mammoth $1.2 billion refinery project in Mexico, because it was "too risky" for the company, the firm's general manager in Mexico said on Wednesday.

Giancorrado Stucchi told Reuters the revamping of northern refinery Cadereyta requires the contractor to finance the three-year project out of its own pocket. State oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) would then pay back the contractor in equal payments plus interest over ten years, he said.
"It is difficult for us to take on the financial risk of a project like that," he said. "The problem is Snam Progetti is not willing to take on a construction risk for three years."
He said banks would agree to finance the project, but the constructor would still need to provide the guarantees for the loan.
Snam Progetti is partly owned by Italy's state oil company Snam and controlled by ENI group.
"The company's capital share was $300 million to $350 million in 1996. So the project's numbers are too big a risk for us," he said.
"We're not used to working on this basis. We're good at jobs when the financing of projects is by banks or by the company."
Snam Progetti recently completed construction of a new unit at Pemex's Tula refinery that has the capacity to process 42,000 barrels per day (bpd) of cleaner fuel oil, lowering the sulphur content.
The project was financed 75 percent by the Japanese government and 25 percent from Pemex, Stucchi said.

He said some of Snam Progetti's larger competitors could be in a better position to bid for the Cadereyta project. The project includes the construction of nine to 10 new plants, the renovation and expansion of nine plants and the construction of four sales terminals.
The only consortia that has publically announced it will bid for Cadereyta is Mexican builder Bufete Industrial with Japanese Mitsubishi Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and Itochu Corp.

Other interested bidders include: South Korea's Sunkyong, U.S. contractor Raytheon Corp ; Mexican builder Empresas ICA and U.S. partner Fluor Daniel ; Italy's Technipetrol; Brazil's Construtora Norbeto Odebrecht SA ; Japan's Chiyoda Corp and Germany's Siemens AG.
Some reports have said Pemex is trying to negotiate with companies to persuade them to stay in the bidding. Further associations may also be in the works.
He added that Pemex paid regularly and was a good client for whom Snam Progetti would like to work again.
"There should be opportunities because Pemex plans to upgrade and revamp all six of its refineries," he said. "I hope there will be a chance for us to obtain other projects."
The company is eyeing bids for projects that should be tendered in 1998, he said.
